causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (L-DOPA --DOPA decarboxylase--> dopamine); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (AADC/DDC deficiency: reduced dopamine and its CSF metabolite HVA); natural human LoF (AADC deficiency) causes combined dopamine/serotonin deficiency with reduced CSF dopamine/HVA, confirming do(AADC)->CSF dopamine sign '+' (PMC10530573; OMIM 608643)
causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.mechanism: aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase produces dopamine from L-DOPA; higher enzyme activity raises CNS dopamine synthesis (AADC deficiency lowers CSF dopamine/HVA)

causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.evidence: Swoboda KJ et al., Ann Neurol 2003 (AADC deficiency: profoundly reduced plasma catecholamines — dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine all markedly low); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (AADC/DDC deficiency, OMIM 608643: absent catecholamine synthesis); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (catecholamine biosynthesis: all catecholamines derive from dopamine produced by AADC) | intervention: AADC deficiency (DDC gene LoF, OMIM 608643): do(aadc_activity=low) -> plasma_catecholamines falls to near zero
causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.mechanism: AADC is the obligate rate-limiting enzyme for synthesis of all three major catecholamines (dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine) by decarboxylating L-DOPA to dopamine (the common precursor); higher AADC activity raises the total plasma catecholamine pool; AADC deficiency profoundly reduces all plasma catecholamines

causal:influence:acid_alpha_glucosidase_.evidence: Pompe disease (GSD II, OMIM:232300); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, glycogen metabolism; Hirschhorn & Reuser in OMMBID 'Glycogen Storage Disease Type II' (GAA deficiency -> lysosomal glycogen accumulation in muscle); PMC4103853 (pharmacological chaperone AT2220 + ERT reduce glycogen in Pompe mice, confirming GAA activity -> muscle glycogen sign). | intervention: GBA2 / GAA loss-of-function (Pompe disease): do(acid_alpha_glucosidase_activity = down) -> muscle glycogen accumulates (up); ERT (alglucosidase alfa): do(GAA activity = up) -> muscle glycogen falls (down).
causal:influence:acid_alpha_glucosidase_.mechanism: Lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) cleaves alpha-1,4- and alpha-1,6-glucosidic bonds in glycogen within the lysosome of muscle cells; loss of GAA activity (Pompe disease / GSD II) prevents lysosomal glycogen degradation, causing glycogen accumulation in skeletal muscle and heart. Enzyme replacement therapy with alglucosidase alfa (recombinant GAA) reduces muscle glycogen content, confirming the direct interventional relationship.

causal:influence:ada2_activity:positive:.evidence: Rosen et al., N Engl J Med 2014 (DADA2 = ADA2 deficiency, OMIM 615688: ADA2 catalyzes adenosine -> inosine in plasma); GeneReviews DADA2 (NBK544951): ADA2 deaminates adenosine and 2'-deoxyadenosine to inosine and deoxyinosine. | intervention: do(ADA2 GoF/LoF) — ADA2 activity is the rate-limiting producer of plasma inosine from adenosine
causal:influence:ada2_activity:positive:.mechanism: ADA2 (adenosine deaminase 2) deaminates extracellular adenosine to inosine in plasma; more ADA2 activity produces more plasma inosine. In DADA2 (ADA2 deficiency), inosine production from adenosine falls, and plasma adenosine rises while plasma inosine falls.

causal:influence:adenosine_deaminase_act.mechanism: ADA deaminates (deoxy)adenosine; ADA loss causes dAdo accumulation and urinary excretion (ADA-SCID).

causal:influence:adenosine_deaminase_act.evidence: Hershfield, Genet Med 2003 (ADA deficiency, OMIM 102700: deoxyadenosine -> dATP toxicity in T-cells); Hirschhorn, Ann NY Acad Sci 1993 (dATP mechanism of T-cell killing in ADA-SCID); PMC209335 (ADA deficiency increases thymic apoptosis via dATP accumulation); Blood 2009 (doi:10.1182/blood-2009-01-160440: ADA treatment approach confirms T-cell selective toxicity). | intervention: do(ADA LoF, ADA-SCID, OMIM 102700): deoxyadenosine not deaminated; dATP accumulates in T-cells; T-cells die by apoptosis; t_cell_immune_activity falls to near zero.
causal:influence:adenosine_deaminase_act.mechanism: ADA (adenosine deaminase) deaminates deoxyadenosine (and adenosine) to deoxyinosine (and inosine). ADA deficiency (ADA-SCID, OMIM 102700) causes deoxyadenosine to accumulate and be phosphorylated to dATP by deoxynucleoside kinases, particularly in T lymphocytes (which have high deoxynucleoside kinase/low 5'-nucleotidase activity). Excess dATP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase (blocking DNA synthesis), inhibits SAH hydrolase (blocking transmethylation), and activates apoptosis signalling in thymocytes. The net effect is selective T-cell destruction, causing severe combined immunodeficiency. Higher ADA activity prevents dATP accumulation, preserving T-cell survival and immune activity.

causal:influence:aicda_deaminase_activit.evidence: HIGM2 (OMIM 605258): absent IgG including IgG4; Muramatsu et al. Cell 2000. | intervention: do(AICDA LoF) — no class-switch to IgG4 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:aicda_deaminase_activit.mechanism: AID is required for class-switch recombination; AID deficiency abolishes IgG4 production.

causal:influence:aldh7a1_activity:positi.evidence: GeneReviews NBK1486 (Pyridoxine-Dependent Epilepsy, ALDH7A1): 'P6C inactivates PLP and leads to a lifelong hyperphysiologic pyridoxine demand'; AADC secondary deficiency is documented as a consequence. Mills PB et al. Biochem J 2006 — pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy (antiquitin/ALDH7A1 deficiency): P6C condensation with PLP, PLP-dependent enzyme (AADC, GABA-T) deficiency confirmed. OMIM 266100 (pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy). pdeonline.org/resources/PDE-review-MGM.pdf — mechanism of PLP trapping by P6C leading to secondary neurotransmitter synthesis defects. | intervention: do(ALDH7A1 biallelic LoF) = pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy, OMIM 266100: P6C accumulates → PLP trapped → AADC activity reduced | intervention: do(ALDH7A1 biallelic LoF) — pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy (PDE), OMIM 266100
causal:influence:aldh7a1_activity:positi.mechanism: Alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH7A1 / antiquitin) oxidises alpha-AASA to alpha-aminoadipate. ALDH7A1 LoF (pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy, PDE) causes alpha-AASA and its cyclic Schiff base piperideine-6-carboxylate (P6C) to accumulate. P6C condenses with pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) via a Knoevenagel adduction, forming a covalent P6C-PLP adduct that severely depletes bioavailable PLP. Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC/DDC) requires PLP as its obligatory cofactor; PLP depletion reduces AADC activity, causing secondary AADC deficiency with reduced synthesis of dopamine and serotonin. Sign: more ALDH7A1 → less P6C → less PLP trapping → more AADC activity (do(ALDH7A1 LoF) = AADC activity falls).

causal:influence:pnmt_activity:positive:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (epinephrine biosynthesis: norepinephrine -PNMT-> epinephrine, last step in catecholamine pathway); Wurtman & Axelrod (1966) Sci Am 214:100-106 (PNMT induction by adrenal cortex; PNMT controls adrenal epinephrine); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (catecholamine biosynthesis enzymes and CSF metabolite patterns). Intervention: do(PNMT modulation). | intervention: perturbation or genetic modulation of PNMT activity controlling adrenal epinephrine synthesis
causal:influence:pnmt_activity:positive:.mechanism: Phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PNMT) catalyzes the final step of catecholamine biosynthesis: N-methylation of norepinephrine to epinephrine in adrenal medullary chromaffin cells and PNMT-positive neurons (C1-C3 brainstem). PNMT activity directly controls adrenal epinephrine synthesis and secretion; higher PNMT activity yields more epinephrine in plasma. PNMT deficiency or suppression (e.g., in pheochromocytoma-associated NE excess) causes low plasma epinephrine.

causal:influence:prodh_activity:negative.evidence: Hyperprolinemia type I (PRODH deficiency, OMIM 239500) — elevated plasma and CSF proline; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (hyperprolinemia type I: PRODH deficiency, plasma and CSF proline elevated); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (proline catabolism: proline --PRODH--> P5C --P5C dehydrogenase--> glutamate). | intervention: do(PRODH LoF) — hyperprolinemia type I
causal:influence:prodh_activity:negative.mechanism: Proline dehydrogenase 1 (PRODH) is the mitochondrial enzyme that oxidizes proline to pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C), the first step in proline catabolism; PRODH deficiency (hyperprolinemia type I) blocks proline degradation, causing proline to accumulate in plasma and CSF.

causal:influence:progesterone:negative:p.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-166 (28.5: Changes During Pregnancy, Labor, and Birth): 'Like estrogen, progesterone suppresses FSH and LH.' | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-43.3 (43.3: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Gametogenesis): 'Progesterone assists in endometrial regrowth and inhibition of FSH and LH release.' causal:influence:progesterone:negative:p.mechanism: Progesterone directly suppresses pituitary FSH secretion (parallel to estradiol), preventing ovulation during pregnancy

causal:influence:pulmonary_capillary_blo.mechanism: more blood in pulmonary capillaries provides more hemoglobin/surface for gas uptake, raising diffusing capacity

causal:influence:pulmonary_vascular_resi.mechanism: generalized pulmonary vasoconstriction (raised resistance) raises pulmonary arterial pressure at fixed flow

causal:influence:purine_nucleoside_phosp.evidence: PNP deficiency OMIM 613179; Stoop et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 1977 (elevated urinary inosine and guanosine). | intervention: do(PNP LoF) — plasma guanosine rises; urinary excretion increases
causal:influence:purine_nucleoside_phosp.mechanism: PNP LoF causes guanosine accumulation in plasma; elevated plasma guanosine is filtered and excreted in urine (urinary guanosine rises in PNP deficiency).

causal:influence:renal_glutaminase_activ.evidence: Glutaminase deficiency (EIEE71), OMIM:617924 — GLS LoF causes markedly elevated plasma glutamine; patients present with severe neurodevelopmental disorder and hyperammonemia
causal:influence:renal_glutaminase_activ.mechanism: RHEA:15889 (EC 3.5.1.2): L-glutamine + H2O = L-glutamate + NH4(+); L-glutamine is the substrate; GLS LoF impairs glutamine catabolism, causing systemic glutamine accumulation

causal:influence:renal_perfusion_pressur.evidence: "Increases in arterial pressure tend to raise peritubular capillary hydrostatic pressure" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 27 (Urine Formation II) Table 27-2, p 341
causal:influence:renal_perfusion_pressur.mechanism: increased renal arterial pressure -> raised peritubular (and vasa recta) capillary hydrostatic pressure (buffered by autoregulation) -> feeds pressure-natriuresis reduction in reabsorption (Table 27-2: up Arterial Pressure -> up Pc)

causal:influence:right_atrial_pressure:n.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.20 (Cardiac Output, Venous Return, and Their Regulation) §Normal Venous Return Curve: “the backward force of the rising atrial pressure on the veins of the systemic circulation decreases venous return of blood to the heart.”
causal:influence:right_atrial_pressure:n.mechanism: rising right-atrial pressure exerts a backward force on the veins (reduces the Psf–PRA pressure gradient), impeding flow of blood from the systemic veins into the right atrium

causal:influence:sarcolemmal_permeabilit.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (serum CK activity assay used to diagnose/monitor muscular dystrophies and rhabdomyolysis); OMIM 310200; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (CK catalytic mechanism). | intervention: do(sarcolemmal_permeability ↑) — Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD LoF)
causal:influence:sarcolemmal_permeabilit.mechanism: Serum creatine kinase catalytic activity rises in parallel with total CK protein concentration when muscle CK leaks through a damaged sarcolemma; the enzyme retains activity in circulation, so serum CK activity faithfully tracks the leakage event.

causal:influence:sarcolemmal_permeabilit.evidence: Casciola-Rosen et al. PMC3786178 (isolated elevated serum aldolase in myositis patients; ALDOA leaks from damaged regenerating muscle fibres); UpToDate 'Rhabdomyolysis' (aldolase listed among muscle enzymes elevated in rhabdomyolysis); Harrison's 'Polymyositis and Dermatomyositis' (serum aldolase elevation); OMIM 310200. | intervention: do(sarcolemmal_permeability ↑) — Duchenne MD / inflammatory myopathy paradigm
causal:influence:sarcolemmal_permeabilit.mechanism: Aldolase A (ALDOA) is the muscle isoform of fructose-bisphosphate aldolase; it is a cytosolic glycolytic enzyme that leaks into plasma when the sarcolemma is damaged. Elevated serum aldolase is found in inflammatory myopathies, rhabdomyolysis and muscular dystrophies.

causal:influence:sardh_activity:negative.evidence: Sarcosinemia (SARDH deficiency, OMIM 268900) — elevated plasma and CSF sarcosine (N-methylglycine); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (sarcosinemia: SARDH deficiency, sarcosine elevated in plasma, urine, and CSF); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (sarcosine dehydrogenase in the one-carbon/folate cycle; sarcosine -> glycine by SARDH). | intervention: do(SARDH LoF) — sarcosinemia
causal:influence:sardh_activity:negative.mechanism: Sarcosine dehydrogenase (SARDH) catabolizes sarcosine (N-methylglycine) to glycine + formaldehyde in the mitochondria; SARDH deficiency (sarcosinemia) abolishes this conversion, causing sarcosine to accumulate in plasma and CSF.

causal:influence:skeletal_muscle_blood_f.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 12th edition; (Ch. 20, Cardiac Output, Venous Return, and Their Regulation); “The venous return to the heart is the sum of all the local blood flows through all the individual tissue segments of the peripheral circulation. Therefore, it follows that cardiac output regulation is the sum of all the local blood flow regulations.” | Local tissue blood flow (here skeletal-muscle blood flow) sums into venous return and thereby sets cardiac output, supporting skeletal_muscle_blood_flow -> cardiac_output with sign +.
causal:influence:skeletal_muscle_blood_f.mechanism: Skeletal-muscle vasodilation (e.g. driven by intracellular ATP/creatine-phosphate depletion during work) increases local muscle blood flow; because venous return is the sum of all local tissue blood flows, increasing muscle blood flow raises venous return and therefore cardiac output - the Guyton local-flow control of cardiac output.

causal:influence:skin_blood_flow:negativ.evidence: Rowell 1974 (cutaneous vasodilation reduces TPR during heat stress)
causal:influence:skin_blood_flow:negativ.mechanism: cutaneous vasodilation adds a low-resistance parallel bed, lowering systemic vascular resistance

causal:influence:slc6a19_activity:negati.evidence: Hartnup disease OMIM 234500; Merck Manual Hartnup: glutamine listed among neutral amino acids elevated in urine in Hartnup; PMC7165679 (SLC6A19 neutral amino acid transporter review). | intervention: do(SLC6A19 loss-of-function) — Hartnup disease OMIM 234500
causal:influence:slc6a19_activity:negati.mechanism: SLC6A19 (B0AT1) reabsorbs neutral amino acids including glutamine in the renal proximal tubule. Hartnup disease (SLC6A19 LoF) causes glutamine to appear in elevated amounts in urine. do(SLC6A19 LoF) -> urinary glutamine rises.

causal:influence:somatostatin:negative:g.mechanism: somatostatin acts on parietal cells and G-cells via SSTRs to inhibit gastric acid secretion; somatostatin analogues used clinically to reduce gastrointestinal secretions

causal:influence:somatostatin:negative:s.evidence: "Growth hormone inhibitory hormone (somatostatin)" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 75, p. 925
causal:influence:somatostatin:negative:s.mechanism: hypothalamic somatostatin (growth-hormone inhibitory hormone) suppresses somatotroph GH secretion

(1999) Cell 98:181, PubMed 10428030 (opened) — Stat5a-/-5b-/- knockout abolishes immediate-early Bcl-xL induction in erythroid cells and STAT5 binds the Bcl-X promoter directly, i.e. do(STAT5 LoF) -> Bcl-xL down. Adlung et al. (2021) Cell Reports 36:109507 (STAT5-driven anti-apoptotic survival program in erythroid progenitors). Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (EPO promotes erythroid survival). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:stat5_activity:positive.mechanism: pSTAT5 transcriptionally induces the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-xL (quality: pSTAT5 activity -> disposition: STAT5 binding at the BCL2L1 promoter -> process: Bcl-xL transcription -> quality: Bcl-xL protein level)

causal:influence:stroke_volume:negative:.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep (EDV = ESV + venous filling; greater emptying lowers carried-over volume); Guyton & Hall (ventricular volume balance over the cardiac cycle)
causal:influence:stroke_volume:negative:.mechanism: at a given filling rate, greater ejection lowers the residual (end-systolic) volume carried into the next diastole, reducing end-diastolic volume — the volume-draining arm that, with venous filling, closes the ventricular volume balance

causal:influence:stroke_volume:positive:.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology 3rd ed., 'Arterial pressure' (pulse pressure ~ SV / arterial compliance). | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-112 (20.3: Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance): 'a low or narrow [pulse pressure] may occur in patients with a low stroke volume... a high or wide pulse pressure is common in healthy people following strenuous exercise, when...pulse pressure...may increase...as stroke volume increases.'
causal:influence:stroke_volume:positive:.mechanism: Pulse pressure = systolic - diastolic arterial pressure; for a given arterial compliance, a larger ejected stroke volume per beat raises systolic pressure more than diastolic, widening pulse pressure.

causal:influence:t2_thiolase_activity:ne.evidence: Beta-ketothiolase / T2 deficiency (alpha-methylacetoacetic aciduria; OMIM 203750): elevated urinary ketone bodies including acetoacetate during metabolic crisis is a key marker (OMIM 203750; PMC6790690 'Mutation update on ACAT1 variants associated with T2 deficiency'; PMC8900828 case report). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry ch. 17 (ketone body metabolism; T2 thiolase in acetoacetyl-CoA utilization). | intervention: do(ACAT1 LoF) -> T2 thiolase activity falls -> acetoacetyl-CoA not cleaved -> acetoacetate accumulates -> urinary acetoacetate elevated
causal:influence:t2_thiolase_activity:ne.mechanism: Mitochondrial acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (T2/ACAT1) catalyzes the thiolytic cleavage of acetoacetyl-CoA to two acetyl-CoA molecules (ketone body utilization step in peripheral tissues) and also the cleavage of 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA in isoleucine catabolism. T2 deficiency impairs ketone body utilization, causing acetoacetyl-CoA and acetoacetate to accumulate and be excreted. More T2 activity clears acetoacetate/acetoacetyl-CoA faster.

causal:influence:telomerase_activity:pos.evidence: Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-7.7 (Telomeres - Undeclared): 'Telomerase is a large holoenzyme that acts as a reverse transcriptase, reading a self-contained RNA template to add on telomere sequence to the 3’ ends of linear chromosomes' and 'while telomerases are active, the 3’ ends can be extended'
causal:influence:telomerase_activity:pos.mechanism: Telomerase acts as a reverse transcriptase reading its self-contained RNA template to add telomeric repeat sequences to the 3' ends of linear chromosomes, thereby extending telomere length

causal:influence:telomere_length:positiv.evidence: Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-7.7 (Telomeres): 'As cells divide, the telomeres shorten, and eventually signal the cell to stop dividing.' Dyskeratosis congenita (OMIM #305000): LoF mutations in TERT/DKC1 reduce telomerase activity and shorten telomeres, causing premature stem-cell exhaustion and tissue failure. Harley et al. 1990 Nature 345:458 (PMID 2342578) (telomere shortening limits replicative lifespan). | intervention: genetic LoF of TERT or DKC1 (dyskeratosis congenita) shortens telomeres and reduces replicative capacity; overexpression of telomerase in primary cells extends replicative lifespan (Bodnar et al. 1998 Science 279:349 PMID 9454332) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:telomere_length:positiv.mechanism: Each somatic cell division shortens telomeres by 50-200 bp; when telomeres reach a critically short length they trigger DNA-damage responses (p53/p21 pathway) that induce replicative senescence or apoptosis, limiting the total number of cell divisions (Hayflick limit). Longer initial telomere length allows more doublings before reaching the senescence threshold.

causal:influence:testosterone:positive:b.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.80 (Reproductive and Hormonal Functions of the Male (and Function of the Pineal Gland)) §Testosterone Increases Bone Matrix and Causes Calcium Retention: “testosterone increases the total quantity of bone matrix and causes calcium retention”
causal:influence:testosterone:positive:b.mechanism: testosterone increases bone matrix deposition and calcium retention, raising skeletal bone mass

causal:influence:testosterone:positive:m.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.72 (Energetics and Metabolic Rate) §Male Sex Hormone Increases Metabolic Rate: “The male sex hormone testosterone can increase the metabolic rate about 10 to 15 per cent.”
causal:influence:testosterone:positive:m.mechanism: androgen-receptor activation raising cellular oxidative metabolic rate (beyond the muscle-mass route)

causal:influence:thrombin:positive:plate.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep (thrombin-induced platelet activation, PAR receptors); Panteleev 2010 BioModels BIOMD0000000740 (platelet/surface-dependent thrombin generation) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-005 (1.6: Homeostasis): 'As each step of clotting occurs, it stimulates the release of more clotting substances' — positive feedback amplification of clotting cascade; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-104 (18.6: Hemostasis): 'activated platelet level / procoagulant surface ... thrombin [activates] platelets (via PAR receptors)'; Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-11.1.3 (Peripheral Proteins): '…or when thrombin activates platelet receptors' — thrombin-mediated platelet receptor activation corroborated; Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-7.2.5 (Glycosaminoglycans - Heteropolysaccharides with Disaccharide Repeating Units): 'thrombin, which cleaves fibrinogen and activates platelets to form clots' — corroborates thrombin activating platelets
causal:influence:thrombin:positive:plate.mechanism: thrombin cleaves platelet PAR-1/PAR-4 receptors, activating platelets and exposing procoagulant phosphatidylserine surface for assembly of tenase/prothrombinase complexes

causal:influence:tissue_o2_extraction:ne.evidence: oxygen extraction from the blood must increase to meet the metabolic needs, thereby decreasing the mixed venous P O2 and O2 concentration
causal:influence:tissue_o2_extraction:ne.mechanism: increased O2 extraction lowers mixed venous PO2 and O2 content

causal:influence:transaldolase_activity:.evidence: Transaldolase deficiency OMIM 606003; Wamelink et al. 2001 AJHG (PMID 11283793; elevated D-arabitol and ribitol in plasma); Williams et al. 2019 JIMD ('elevated arabitol, ribitol, and erythritol in urine and plasma in all patients'); Mayo Clinic Labs TALDO panel (arabitol and ribitol elevated) | intervention: do(TALDO1 LoF) -> plasma arabinitol UP (primary diagnostic metabolite) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:transaldolase_activity:.mechanism: TALDO1 deficiency causes xylulose-5-P and related C5 intermediates to accumulate; xylulose-5-P is reduced to arabinitol (D-arabitol). Elevated plasma arabinitol (D-arabitol) is a hallmark metabolite of transaldolase deficiency.

causal:influence:urinary_d_lactate:negat.evidence: PMID 35783896; (Abstract); “Systemic absorption of D-lactic acid results in anion-gap metabolic acidosis (AGMA), LA, and neurologic symptoms.” | absorbed D-lactic acid causes anion-gap metabolic acidosis (decreased pH), so increased D-lactate body/urine load lowers arterial pH (sign -) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:urinary_d_lactate:negat.mechanism: D-lactate (whose urinary excretion tracks systemic D-lactate load) is a metabolic acid; systemic absorption produces anion-gap metabolic acidosis, lowering arterial blood pH

causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_iii_sy.evidence: Harrison's PIM, The Porphyrias (CEP: UROS deficiency, elevated erythrocyte coproporphyrin I); GeneReviews NBK154652 (CEP: ‘elevated levels of uroporphyrin I and coproporphyrin I in erythrocytes’). OMIM 263700 (CEP, UROS LoF). | intervention: UROS (uroporphyrinogen-III synthase) loss-of-function (congenital erythropoietic porphyria, OMIM 263700)
causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_iii_sy.mechanism: UROS deficiency (congenital erythropoietic porphyria, CEP) shunts hydroxymethylbilane to uroporphyrinogen I, which is further converted non-enzymatically to coproporphyrin I. Coproporphyrin I accumulates in erythrocytes.

causal:influence:vsm_cgmp_level:negative.mechanism: cGMP inhibits calcium channels, preventing a rise in intracellular calcium concentration

production:production-da5a4020edd77763a1.evidence: CB-PHY-006 (production lift, adrenal zona reticularis -> plasma DHEA-S). SULT2A1 is localized to the zona reticularis and sulfates DHEA at C3beta to DHEA-S, quantitatively the dominant adrenal secretory steroid (~95-100% adrenal origin): PAPSS2/SULT2A1 adrenal DHEA-sulfation coupling, PMC6016456. "DHEA-S is secreted by the adrenal zona reticularis; adrenarche = maturation of the zona reticularis with rising DHEAS" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed. (ISBN:9780323297387). Structural mirror of the deployed zona_glomerulosa_cell_aldosterone_secretion -> aldosterone production edge.
production:production-da5a4020edd77763a1.mechanism: adrenal zona reticularis cells sulfate DHEA intracellularly via SULT2A1 (DHEA-preferring sulfotransferase) and secrete DHEA-sulfate; the zona reticularis secretion rate sets the plasma DHEA-S pool. Produced entity is the sulfated ester DHEA-S (CHEBI:16814), NOT DHEA (CHEBI:28689) — no conflation
